paragraphs: Book Systems sells library automation and asset tracking software. Its main product, Atriuum, is cloud-based automation designed for public, academic, school and special libraries. It gathers circulation, cataloging, reporting and a modern patron catalog in one system.

The system runs in a browser with no per-seat licensing or installs. Libraries get Z39.50 copy cataloging, batch processing for bulk records, and offline circulation that keeps working without an internet connection. RFID support and barcode scanning handle checkouts. It connects to digital content providers including OverDrive, hoopla, CloudLibrary and MackinVIA. Patrons can sign in once through Google, ClassLink or Clever. A staff interface called Stax organizes the work into role-based workspaces. The patron catalog draws on linked data from the Library of Congress.

The company says it has been delivering this software for over 35 years. Its buyers range from public communities and academic institutions to K-12 schools, churches and special collections. Hosting is offered as a subscription, and the company performs daily database backups. Staff exhibit at library conferences, among them the Association for Rural & Small Libraries.

quote.text: Stax is not a separate system. It is a new way to interact with your existing Atriuum data.
